scout.purpose: Networking correctness begins with HTTP method, URI, representation, status, cache, and idempotency semantics rather than a Retrofit annotation.
scout.realWorldUse: Every API call crosses unreliable networks and independent server evolution, so clients must interpret protocol outcomes without assuming success-shaped JSON.
scout.outcome: Design a resource request, classify status families, use headers deliberately, and distinguish safe, idempotent, and retryable operations.

blocks.text: A request combines method, target URI, headers, and optional body; a response combines status, headers, and optional representation. GET retrieves, POST commonly creates or invokes, PUT replaces at a known target, PATCH partially updates, and DELETE removes according to the API contract. Method names do not guarantee a good server design, but they provide shared semantics for caches, intermediaries, and retries. HTTPS protects transport; never place credentials or private values in URLs that may be logged.

blocks.title: Protocol decision
rows: Use server-supported idempotency key before retry

sections.title: Status and headers are part of the result

blocks.text: Treat 2xx as successful status families while respecting cases such as 204 with no body. Redirects, 4xx client outcomes, and 5xx server failures need separate policies. 401 concerns authentication, 403 authorization, 404 absence, 409 conflict, 429 rate limits, and Retry-After can guide waiting. Content-Type describes the body representation and Accept expresses client preference. Cache-Control, ETag, and If-None-Match enable validation instead of always downloading full content.

blocks.title: Protocol semantics precede client code
blocks.text: A library cannot decide whether an operation is safe to repeat or cache.

sections.title: Retry safety depends on operation semantics

blocks.text: Safe methods do not intend state change; idempotent methods can be repeated with the same intended effect, though logging or counters may still vary. Retrying a timed-out non-idempotent POST can duplicate a purchase unless the API supports an idempotency key. Network success does not guarantee business success, and HTTP failure may contain structured error details. Record request correlation and timing without bodies, tokens, or personal data. Test malformed, empty, unexpected, and forward-compatible responses.

Production readiness requires evidence beyond a happy-path demonstration. State the owner and lifetime of every mutable value, the expected response to failure or cancellation, and the behaviour after recreation or a second simultaneous request. Exercise long and translated content, large font scale, alternate input, slow dependencies, and rapid repeated actions wherever they apply. Prefer deterministic unit tests for pure logic, integration tests at library and protocol boundaries, and device tests when platform lifecycle, rendering, accessibility, or system UI is part of the contract. Do not hide a missing decision behind a generic helper. A future engineer should be able to identify what may run concurrently, what survives, what is authoritative, and which evidence proves the implementation remains correct.

steps.label: Define contract
steps.detail: Name ownership, lifetime, inputs, outputs, failure, and cancellation.

steps.label: Implement
steps.detail: Choose the smallest API that preserves those semantics.

steps.label: Exercise boundaries
steps.detail: Test absence, failure, recreation, concurrency, and unusual input.

steps.label: Collect evidence
steps.detail: Use semantics, deterministic tests, traces, or protocol inspection.

steps.label: Harden
steps.detail: Fix the demonstrated risk and document the remaining trade-off.

inspect.title: Stop retrying an unsafe purchase blindly
walkthrough: A timeout may happen after the server accepted the purchase but before the client saw the response.
Repeating POST can create duplicate charges or orders.
Use a stable idempotency key and server contract, then query authoritative outcome.
inspect.expectedOutput: Repeated transport attempts correspond to one logical purchase.

trap_check.mistake: Parsing every non-2xx response as the success DTO.
trap_check.why: Error bodies and empty responses follow different schemas.
trap_check.fix: Branch on status and decode typed success or failure representations separately.

trap_check.mistake: Adding abstraction or optimisation before defining the failure.
trap_check.why: The code becomes harder while ownership, correctness, or measured cost remains unresolved.
trap_check.fix: First write a boundary test or collect evidence that identifies the real defect.

challenge_intro.task: Write and test the HTTP contract for article listing, conditional refresh, article lookup, bookmarking, conflict, rate limit, and typed error responses.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Every method and status has explicit body semantics. Cache validators and sensitive-header policy are defined. Retry safety is documented per operation.
